notes.母湯: Spells the sound of Taiwanese 毋通 m̄-thang, "must not" — the characters are only the sound.
notes.歸剛: Spells Taiwanese 規工 kui-kang, "the whole day"; the meme adds 欸 (歸剛欸).
notes.阿雜: A Taiwanese word (a-tsa̍p) written with sound-alike characters.
notes.盤子: Taiwanese phân-á, "plate": someone easily served up — a sucker.
notes.蛤: Just the sound of the Taiwanese "hannh?"; the character means clam.
notes.魯蛇: Sound-spelling of English "loser" — 魯 and 蛇 carry no meaning here.
notes.吃土: Literally "eating dirt": nothing left to spend on food.
notes.爆雷: Taiwan says 爆雷／有雷／防雷; 劇透 is the China term you will also see online.
notes.飯糰: Sticky rice wrapped around 油條 youtiao, pickled radish and pork floss.
notes.有雷: The warning tag on PTT / Dcard threads; 防雷 marks a spoiler-free zone.
notes.是在哈囉: Sarcastic; Dcard / PTT slang from around 2019.
notes.泡麵番: As long as it takes to cook instant noodles: a three-minute episode.
notes.機車: Literally a scooter. Calling someone 機車 has nothing to do with riding one.
notes.拍謝: A Taiwanese apology written with Mandarin characters for the sound; nobody reads it as pāixiè.
notes.秀逗: From the English "short" by way of Japanese ショート — a short circuit.
notes.踹共: 出來講 said fast in Taiwanese, then written back in Mandarin characters.
notes.犁田: Literally ploughing a field — what your body does to the tarmac.
notes.北七: 白痴 said in Taiwanese, then written back with the characters that carry the sound.
notes.沙發: From the English "sofa": the first person to sit down in the thread.
notes.頭香: From the first stick of incense of the new year at a temple: the same race to be first.
notes.網路: Taiwan says 網路 where the mainland says 網絡.
notes.甜不辣: From the Japanese てんぷら, written with characters that carry the sound.
notes.乳酪: Taiwan says rǔ luò where the mainland says rǔ lào.
notes.佛跳牆: The name says even a monk would climb the wall for it.

variantNotes.藉口: 藉口 is the Taiwan standard spelling; 借口 is what most people type online.
variantNotes.阿們: Protestant churches write 阿們; Catholic ones write 阿門.
variantNotes.飯糰: Shops write 飯糰 or 飯團; both are common.
variantNotes.豆干: Menus write 豆干 or 豆乾; both are common.
